summary: a scientific task's tolerance by the person's standing rule: the reference's stated uncertainty, otherwise the larger of half a unit in its last printed digit and the run's own numerical error

inputs.name: printed
inputs.meaning: the reference value as its source prints it, as text, its last digit kept as printed (a trailing zero included); in the quantity's unit

inputs.name: stated_uncertainty
inputs.meaning: the uncertainty the source states for that value, in the quantity's unit, or null where it states none

inputs.name: run_numerical_error
inputs.meaning: the run's own numerical error of the quantity, in its unit, as an estimating skill gave it through the runner (the difference between two resolutions, or the standard error of a series the run produced); null where it was not estimated

outputs.name: tolerance
outputs.meaning: the tolerance, in the quantity's unit; null, with why, where the inputs give none

outputs.name: from
outputs.meaning: stated_uncertainty, last_printed_digit or run_numerical_error: which of the rule's ways gave it; null where none did

outputs.name: run_error_estimated
outputs.meaning: true when a run's numerical error was handed and weighed, false when it was not estimated and the half-digit branch alone applied, null where the stated uncertainty was taken

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no tolerance was given, or that the run's error was not estimated; else null

validity: one reference value of one quantity. The stated uncertainty, where there is one, is taken as handed: which uncertainty a source states (a standard error, the spread between its refinement levels) is the reader's to say. The last printed digit is read off the text as printed, so a trailing zero counts and a number already stored as a float has lost its printed form; an integer printed with trailing zeros is read as printed. A run's numerical error is taken as handed: estimating it is another skill's. It judges nothing, and a tolerance the person gave overrides it

source.citation: the person's standing rule of 2026-11-18 (docs/ideas/20261118.md, 'Tolerances by a standing rule', amended in 'Yes, run's own error'); JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM), BIPM (read 2026-11-18, https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-jcgm-100-2008-gum)
source.locus: GUM F.2.2.1, The resolution of a digital indication, printed page 64: with a resolution dx the value lies with equal probability between X - dx/2 and X + dx/2; the last printed digit's unit is the resolution, so half of it is the half-width the rule takes

note: v1 made common (every simulation bundle carries it; the person, 2026-11-18; meta_agent/tasks/025), each worked case naming its kind of system, and following the rule as the person amended it the same day ('Yes, run's own error', docs/ideas/20261118.md): without a stated uncertainty the tolerance is the larger of half the last printed digit and the run's own numerical error, and where that error was not estimated the half-digit branch alone applies and the output says so. A build adapts it to an engine as a next version that names the engine and says adapted_from. No value of a source stands behind the worked cases but the person's own example of 1066 K: each is worked by hand in its worked field.
